tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.description: AI pair programmer and coding agent inside your editor and GitHub.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.description: AI-first code editor with agent mode for multi-file changes.
pros: A free plan is available to try the editor.
Cloud agents can run tasks in parallel on their own machines.

Third-party models on paid plans are billed separately at API list price.
Cloud agents and AI code review start on the $30 Premium plan, not the $8 entry plan.
tools.best_for: An AI-first code editor with agent mode for multi-file changes, for developers who want AI inside the editor.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that works in your terminal.
pros: Runs in the terminal, IDE, Slack, web and mobile.
Available for macOS, Linux and Windows.
Sessions can run on your own infrastructure with self-hosted environments.
limitations: There is no free plan for it; Claude Code starts with the Pro plan.
Usage limits apply on every plan.
Heavy daily use points you to Max plans from $100 a month.
tools.best_for: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, suited to handing off multi-step tasks.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.description: OpenAI's cloud and CLI software engineering agent.
pros: Works on the web, in a CLI, an IDE extension and on iOS.
Plus includes automatic code review and a Slack integration.

Usage is shared with ChatGPT Work, so heavy chat use eats into coding.
Older models get retired from ChatGPT sign-in on a set date, so workflows can need updates.
tools.best_for: OpenAI's cloud and CLI software engineering agent, for working on tasks from the terminal or in the cloud.

tools.name: Devin
tools.description: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that runs long tasks in the cloud.
pros: Tests its work on its own Windows, Mac and Linux virtual machines.
Integrates with Slack, Teams, Linear, Jira, GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket.
Enterprise plans can deploy in your own VPC.
limitations: Individual plans cap concurrent sessions at 10.
Usage beyond the plan quota is charged at API pricing.
Team plans cost $80 a month plus $40 per full developer seat.
tools.best_for: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that runs long tasks in the cloud, for well-scoped tickets you want to hand off.

tools.name: Replit Agent
tools.description: Builds and deploys full apps from a natural-language prompt.
pros: The free Starter plan includes daily Agent credits and one published app.
Databases, storage and publishing are part of the same platform.
limitations: Full build, where Agent works more independently, needs a paid Core or Pro plan.
Free published apps go down after 30 days and carry a Replit badge.
Third-party connectors require Core.

tools.best_for: Builds and deploys full apps from a natural-language prompt, handy for prototypes and internal tools.

tools.name: Lovable

pros: Free to start, with 5 daily build credits (up to 30 a month).
Hosting, authentication and payments are handled for you.

limitations: Credit costs in default mode vary with task complexity, so spend is hard to predict.
Monthly credits expire two months after they are issued.
Credits are not refundable.
tools.best_for: Chat-to-build web apps with hosted deployment, for shipping a landing page or simple app without a developer.

tools.name: Elicit

tools.note: The pricing page did not render plan details for us, so only one con is listed.

Google now brands the product as Gemini Notebook, which can make help pages confusing.
tools.best_for: Google's AI notebook grounded in your own sources, for working through documents you've already collected.

tools.name: Clay

It is run by Heritage Services, so check listings independently.

tools.name: GitHub Agentic Workflows
tools.description: Open-source GitHub CLI extension that turns a Markdown task description into a GitHub Actions workflow run by a coding agent, for issue triage, CI failure analysis, docs updates and tests.
pros: Open source (MIT) and generally available on GitHub Free, Team and Enterprise.
Agents run read-only by default in a sandbox, and their writes go through validated safe outputs.
limitations: Using the default Copilot CLI engine requires a Copilot license, and model use is billed separately.

tools.name: Prophecy DataGPT
tools.description: Runs data prep and analysis inside ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot, showing each result as a visual workflow you can check before it ships as code on your data platform.
pros: Works inside ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot, or in Prophecy's own app.
Free Starter plan with no credit card needed.
limitations: The Professional plan is $150 per user per month, and larger plans are priced through sales.

tools.name: DeepSeek dsh-superagent
tools.description: DeepSeek's MIT-licensed research prototype of a proactive coding agent that watches one GitHub repo, takes requests from allowed people and answers with pull requests.
pros: MIT-licensed and free to run with the model you configure.
Auto-merge is off by default, and you control who can assign it work.
limitations: DeepSeek calls it a research prototype, not an official product.
Sessions run with full OS user access, so DeepSeek advises isolating it first.

tools.name: Abacum Abra
tools.description: Abacum's business-planning agent that routes plain-language questions to specialist agents for modeling, variance analysis and reporting on your company's data.
pros: Included at no extra cost for Abacum customers.
Proposals wait for approval and every step is logged.
limitations: Only available inside Abacum's paid planning platform.

tools.name: Cloudbrowser
tools.description: Sandbox0's cloud Chrome for AI agents: each Codex or Claude Code session gets its own browser and desktop in the cloud, with saved profiles and human takeover.
pros: Each session gets its own Chrome, desktop and files, so parallel agents don't collide.
You can open the same browser to sign in or take over, then hand it back to the agent.
Works with local Codex or Claude Code through Playwright, no need to move your agent.
Free plan includes 1 browser-hour per UTC month; paid plans start at Basic for $20/month.
limitations: Free is capped at 1 browser-hour and 1 concurrent browser per UTC month; it pauses at the limit.
After pause and resume, live tabs aren't kept and site logins can still expire.
Doesn't copy your laptop's Chrome logins; you sign in again in the cloud browser.

tools.name: Zerg Client
tools.description: Beta AI coding agent for your terminal and desktop (ZTC): plans a change, edits code, runs tests, and keeps work in named sessions. Use your own model keys or Zerg Router.
pros: Plan mode explores read-only and proposes changes before you run /execute.
Named sessions let you pick work back up across runs.
Bring your own Anthropic or OpenAI key, or log in through Zerg Router; switch models with /model.
Free to evaluate; personal, educational, research and nonprofit use are permitted under its license.
limitations: Still in beta (v0.11.0-beta.1); the desktop app is a preview build with no stable release.
Source-available, not open source. Ongoing company or commercial use needs a signed license, and pricing isn't published.
Desktop app and interactive terminal need an Apple Silicon Mac; Linux and Windows get headless runs only.
Model usage is billed separately through your provider or Zerg Router.

tools.name: Nod
tools.description: n8n Labs' open-source personal agent for Mac and Windows. It runs in a local sandbox with its own browser, works in Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Slack and sites with no integration, and asks before it acts. Bring your own AI provider.
pros: Open source under Apache 2.0 and free; you pay only your model provider, or run a local open-source model.
Works inside a private VM on your computer with its own browser, and confirms before it sends, pays, posts or deletes.
Shows the cost of every task, with a monthly spending limit and a check-in once a task passes $5.
limitations: Research preview from n8n Labs, not part of the core n8n product.
You need your own AI provider (API key or ChatGPT plan), so setup suits technical users.
Stops when your laptop sleeps, each install has one owner, and there's no hosted version yet.

tools.name: Codend
tools.description: AI agent that turns a plain-language task into working code, a live site or a pull request. Each task gets its own cloud sandbox, and repo changes land on a separate branch for review.
pros: Every task runs in its own cloud sandbox, with a live preview, files and terminal you can watch.
Works on its own branch and opens a pull request, so nothing hits main until you merge.
Free to start with welcome credits and daily credits.
limitations: Free credits are limited; heavier use needs a Plus, Pro or Max plan.
Model choice depends on your plan.

tools.name: Vera by AxiomStudio
tools.description: AI code review agent that reviews every pull request on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps, flagging bugs, logic errors and security risks with file and line references.
pros: Reviews pull requests on GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and Azure DevOps.
Findings come with file and line references and are rated Advisory or Blocker.
AxiomStudio says code review is $0 on both free and paid plans, with unlimited reviews and users.
limitations: Autonomous fixes need AxiomStudio's add-on SDLC team.
New launch (Nov 4, 2026), so there's little independent track record yet.

tools.name: Kiro Crew
tools.description: AWS Kiro's open-source development workspace, now with bots: named, long-running agents with their own memory, permissions and schedules that run parallel coding sessions and report back.
pros: Open source under Apache 2.0, runs on Mac, Linux and Windows, locally or remotely.
Bots keep separate memory and only get the tools and permissions you allow.
Schedules, webhooks and CI events can start work while you're away.
limitations: Needs a Kiro account and plan; agent usage counts against your Kiro credits.
You provide the machine it runs on.

tools.name: Mirage by KageX
tools.description: A free, open-source browser extension that red-teams AI systems. An autonomous agent tests a chat UI in a browser tab or an API endpoint, scores findings deterministically, maps them to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, and exports HTML or JSON reports.
pros: Free and open source under the MIT license.
Tests a chat UI in your active tab or a configured API endpoint, with the same attacks on either.
Scoring is deterministic: a win needs a real decoded side-effect, not an LLM grading itself.
Findings map to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, and reports export as HTML or JSON with full transcripts.
Works with Claude, OpenAI, Grok and local Ollama models, as the attacker/judge or as the target.
limitations: You load it as an unpacked Chrome extension from a GitHub release or a local build.
You provide your own model API keys, and usage is billed by the provider.
Only run it against systems you own or are explicitly authorized to test.

tools.name: HumanMirror Guard
tools.description: Screens a proposed AI-agent action before it runs. Free Python and JavaScript Safe Preflight SDK, with 3 preview calls per 24 hours; paid checks are 0.010 USDC on Base, with audit, pilot and enterprise plans. It also offers a remote MCP endpoint at https://humanmirror.fr/api/one/mcp/ and a Clean JSON tool that normalizes malformed JSON for 0.010 USDC per call on Base.
pros: Screens a proposed agent action before it runs; your own runtime still decides whether to execute it.
Free Python and JavaScript SDK, plus 3 preview calls per 24 hours, with no account, card or wallet required.
Paid continuation is 0.010 USDC on Base with explicit wallet approval; using up the free quota does not trigger an automatic charge.
Optional clients for LangGraph, CrewAI, Coinbase AgentKit, AutoGen and custom agents.
limitations: The free preview is bounded and does not check real permissions, payment policy, accounts or third-party tool results; an ALLOW is not a guarantee the action is safe or authorized.
npm and PyPI packages are not published yet; you download the SDK files from the site.
HumanMirror does not sign, pay or execute the action for you.
Team and enterprise pricing is a mix of euro plans and USDC usage, and is spread across several product pages.

tools.name: Agent Garrett
tools.description: A personal cybersecurity agent for suspicious messages, data-broker removal requests, exposure checks and website watching. Plans start at CAD $2.99/month for Chat; the Agent plan is CAD $4.99/month. You can create an account free and review the plan before paying.
pros: Helps investigate suspicious messages, request data-broker removals, check exposure in available breach and dark-web sources, watch public websites you manage, and ask security questions in plain English.
You can create an account free and review your plan before you pay. Card entry is on Stripe's hosted checkout; cancel anytime in Billing, and access continues until the paid period ends.
Paid plans start at CAD $2.99/month for Chat. The Agent plan is CAD $4.99/month and adds broker-removal work, exposure checks and monitoring. Security is CAD $13.37/month and Max is CAD $35/month.
Tools that act on the outside world are proposed for your approval, with the exact tool and inputs shown, before they run.
Enabled cloud monitoring and scheduled tasks can continue after you close the tab, within your plan and available sources.
limitations: Chat at CAD $2.99/month is for questions and research; scheduled monitoring and cases are not included.

The Agent plan includes monthly allowances: 40 AI credits, 40 hosted-compute minutes, 20,000 MCP requests, up to 3 websites, 10 identity targets and 3 saved conversations. When an allowance is used up, the features that depend on it pause; unused allowance is not refunded.
Broker responses and removal results vary. Agent Garrett does not guarantee that a broker will remove your information, or that removed information will not reappear.
Monitoring, searches and alerts can be late, incomplete or wrong, and AI output can be inaccurate. You review findings and approve actions before relying on them.
Subscriptions are billed monthly in advance in Canadian dollars. Payments are not refundable for a partly used month, except where the law requires a refund.

tools.name: AI Agent Cost Calculator
tools.description: A free, no-login calculator that estimates a 30-day model-token bill from official per-token prices. You pick one of 25 models, enter input and output tokens per task and tasks per day; it runs in the browser and does not include tool fees, caching, seats or hosting.
pros: Free, with no login. The calculation runs in the browser, and the numbers you type are not submitted.
Estimates a 30-day model-token bill from official per-million-token prices copied from provider pages. The prices on the page were read November 11, 2026.
Includes 25 models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and xAI.
The page spells out the formula and what is left out, including cached rates, tool-call fees, seats, hosting and tax.
limitations: It prices model tokens only. Cached input, batch or flex rates, tool-call fees, search grounding, seat licenses, hosting, storage, human review and tax are not included, so a real invoice can be lower or higher.
The 30-day figure is the daily cost times 30, not a calendar month.
Only models whose prices were copied from the provider pages are in the dropdown; other providers are left out rather than guessed.

tools.name: CallEez
tools.description: A UK-built AI phone receptionist that answers calls, books appointments into a connected calendar, sends SMS and email, and can transfer urgent calls. You can create and test an agent in the browser for free, with no card and no phone number. Live answering needs a 7-day trial (card required) or a paid plan; standard plans start at £19/month excl. VAT.
pros: Answers calls 24/7, books appointments into a connected calendar, sends SMS and email to callers, and can transfer urgent calls. Recordings, transcripts and a dedicated phone number are included on every plan, subject to number availability and call credit.
You can create an agent and test it in the browser for free, with no card. The free test includes a limited number of test minutes and does not include a phone number.

Eligible accounts can try a standard plan free for 7 days, with 30 call minutes, 15 SMS, 1 AI receptionist and a phone number. A verified email and card are required. Cancel before the trial ends to avoid the charge.

Standard plans start at £19/month excl. VAT for Beginner (50 minutes, 20 SMS, 1 receptionist). Growth is £89/month and Business is £159/month. Every standard plan includes the same core features; plans differ on minutes, texts, agents and the extras on each card. You can cancel anytime; access continues until the end of the billing period.
You can route an existing business number to the agent after hours, during busy periods, or 24/7, in addition to the included CallEez number.
limitations: Live call answering needs an active trial or plan with call credit. Phone numbers are leased, assigned subject to availability, and may be reassigned after cancellation.

Prices are excl. VAT and billed monthly in advance. Unused monthly plan allowances do not roll over. No refunds are issued for partial months. The 7-day trial converts to the paid plan unless you cancel first; one trial per person or business, and bespoke plans are excluded.

Extra minutes can be topped up at 28p a minute. No extra credit packs are available during the trial. Bookings need a connected calendar, SMS uses the plan's allowance, and call transfers work once set up.
CallEez does not guarantee the agent will answer every call correctly, capture every detail accurately, or relay information without error.

tools.name: RealtyCrawl
tools.description: Unified real estate data API with a catalog of 206 researched sources and 67 documented operations, plus a public OpenAPI spec and a hosted MCP server so AI agents can inspect and call it.
pros: Eligible new accounts get 500 one-time signup credits, with no payment card.
Agents can use the hosted or local MCP server, an installable skill, or the public OpenAPI file.
Failed provider calls are refunded automatically, and unavailable operations fail without consuming credits.
limitations: The 67 documented operations across 206 sources include preview coverage; a catalog listing does not guarantee live access, so you have to check capabilities for the call you need.
Monthly plan credits expire at the end of the billing cycle and do not roll over. Starter is $15 a month for 2,500 credits, Growth is $49 for 20,000, and Pro is $299 for 150,000.

tools.name: Lumo Desktop
tools.description: Proton's private AI assistant as a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, with Connectors to local files, shell, Proton Mail, Google Drive, Jira and MCP servers, plus scheduled tasks and reusable Skills.
pros: For each connector you choose which actions Lumo runs automatically, which need your approval, and which are blocked.
Proton says Lumo never uses your chats or connected data to train models, and chat history is protected with zero-access encryption.
Schedules run tasks at a set time or on repeat, such as a weekly inbox summary, each with its own permissions.
Proton publishes the source code so anyone can inspect how the tools work.
limitations: Connectors only work in the desktop app, and Proton Mail access goes through Proton Mail Bridge.
Connector actions are set to Auto-approve by default, so you have to tighten permissions yourself.
The free plan limits chats, uploads, image generations and projects; Lumo Plus raises those limits.

tools.name: Caveman Code
tools.description: Coding agent app for Mac and the browser that runs Claude Agent, Codex, Cursor and Caveman's own agent side by side on the plans and API keys you already have, with a harness built to spend fewer tokens.
pros: Free on your own keys and logins; your Claude plan runs as Claude Agent and your ChatGPT plan as Codex.
A "Chief" can start chats, answer their questions and report back when the work is done.
Cloud computers (in beta) let an agent drive a desktop and browser to check its work, and keep going when your laptop closes.
limitations: The cost and token savings (for example 21% less than Codex on Terminal-Bench 4) come from Caveman's own November 2026 runs.
Caveman Code is proprietary; the Caveman CLI, SDKs and skill are the Apache-2.0 parts.
Paid plans are credits: Pro is $20 a month for $20 of credits, and any week or 5-hour window can use at most 35% of a month's credits.
Mac and browser only at launch; a terminal app is listed as next.

tools.name: AgentRun
tools.description: Open-source (Apache-2.0) platform from Parcha Labs, the team behind Grep, that adds learning between runs, durable recovery, reusable workflows and a management console to Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and pi agents.
pros: Free to self-host under Apache-2.0 with your own model keys; start locally with npx @parcha/agentrun.
Repeated steps can become reusable skills and workflows, which are checked and graded before later runs reuse them.
Interrupted runs recover from the saved conversation, files and tool results instead of starting over.
limitations: Launched as an open-source alpha.
You pay your own model and infrastructure costs; the documented Render setup is about $27.50 a month before model, tool and computer usage.
Learning adds its own reflection and grading cost, and savings depend on how much of your work repeats.

tools.name: Hark Pro
tools.description: Personal AI assistant with a built-in computer-use agent, Handoff, that completes web tasks like ordering groceries, booking flights and scheduling appointments. Handoff², released Nov 12, 2026, averages about twice the speed.
pros: Free to use with no ads; every plan has all features, and upgrading only adds usage.
Handoff² finished 82% of Hark's 478-task internal browsing benchmark, up from 73% for v1, in 46% less time per task.
Besides web tasks, Hark Pro handles email, scheduled tasks, Slack tracking and docs.
limitations: Speed and accuracy figures come from Hark's own internal benchmarks.
Handoff² is rolling out to Hark Pro users gradually, starting Nov 12, 2026.
Heavier use needs Hark Pro², which is $20 a month.

tools.name: Daydream Agent
tools.description: Autonomous fashion shopping agent that searches thousands of brands, builds outfits, offers virtual try-on and, with your approval, checks out with participating retailers, in the Daydream iOS app or by text message.
pros: Daydream says the service is completely free to use.
Virtual try-on works from one uploaded photo that you reuse for anything saved to your clothing rack.
Can keep working in the background, for example telling you when a saved item goes on sale or a brand has a new drop.
limitations: Agentic checkout only works with participating brand and retail partners, and each purchase needs your approval.
Launched in the iOS app and by text message only.
